_comment: Serialised story for Section 2 (A1.2), episodes 13-24. Continues 'New in Tashkent': Sarah's first year, Aziz's exams, Kamola's new flat, Bobur's football team. Every episode uses only lexemes taught up to and including its unit.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Sarah, what are you doing these days?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: I am working in two schools this month.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Two schools? That is a lot!

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: I know. I usually work in one, but Mr Karimov is not well.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: I understand. And Aziz?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: He is studying every evening. He is working very hard.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: He always studies hard.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Yes, but he is not sleeping well now.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Do you want some tea? I am making it now.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Yes, please. I think tea is very good.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Excuse me. Where is the post office?

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: Go straight on and turn left at the bank.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Turn left at the bank. And then?

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: Cross the road. The post office is on the corner.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Is it far?

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: No, it is not far. Do not take a taxi.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Thank you! Sarah — from the school. And you are Bobur?

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: Yes! Aziz is my friend. The bus stop is here too.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Good. Which bus goes to the station?

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: Number nine. But do not take it now — walk.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Excuse me, how much is this scarf?

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: The red one is fifty thousand som.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: And the blue one?

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: The blue one is cheap — thirty thousand.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Do you have many scarves?

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: Yes, we have a lot. Green, black, white and brown.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: I would like the green one. Can I try it on?

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: Yes. It is a good size for you.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: I take it. Can I pay by credit card?

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: Yes. Here is your receipt and your change.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Sarah, we have a new teacher at school.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Really? What does he look like?

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: He is tall and thin. He has short dark hair.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Does he wear glasses?

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Yes, and he has a small black beard.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: And what is he like?

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: He is very kind and patient. But he is quiet.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Quiet is good. Our old teacher was not quiet!

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: The students like him. He is not lazy — he is hard-working.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: He looks like a good teacher.

body.speaker: narrator
body.text: Kamola has a new flat. Sarah is there today.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: It is very comfortable! Is this your sofa?

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: No, it is not mine. It is my mother's sofa.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: And whose picture is that?

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: It is my brother's. Aziz draws very well.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: The bedrooms are upstairs?

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Yes. My room is the small one. The big one is my sister's.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Are your neighbours quiet?

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Very quiet. But the street is noisy in the morning.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: My flat is noisy too. Ours is near the market.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Sarah, where were you yesterday?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: I was at home all day. I was very tired.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Were you at work?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: No, but the week was very long.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: There was a party at his house.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: A party? Were there many people?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: There were twenty people! It was his birthday.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: No! I am sorry. I was not there.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: It is not a problem. He was happy — his team was there too.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Two days ago he was nervous. Now he is glad!

body.speaker: narrator
body.text: Aziz had his exam last Monday.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Aziz! How was it?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: I studied for three weeks. I did not sleep much.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: And?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: I finished early. Then I waited for two hours.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Two hours! What did you do?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: I walked in the park. I called my mother.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: What did she say?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: She said, 'Come home and eat.' So I went home.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: And then?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: It came this morning. It was very good!

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Sarah, did you go to Samarkand last week?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Yes, I did! I went by train.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Did you like it?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: I loved it. But I did not have much time.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: How long was the journey?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Two hours. It was fast and very comfortable.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Did you take photos?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: A lot! But I did not take my camera — only my phone.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Did you buy any souvenirs?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: I bought a small one for my mother. It was not expensive.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Did you go alone?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: No, I did not. A tourist guide helped me all day.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Aziz, what are you going to do next year?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: I am going to study at university.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: That is a good plan. What are you going to study?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: My dream is to be a doctor. I hope to study here.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: You are going to be a very good doctor.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: And you? Are you going to stay in Tashkent?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: I think so. I am meeting Mr Karimov on Friday.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Look! It is going to rain.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: We are going to be cold! Let us walk fast.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: The bus is coming. We are not going to walk!

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: Aziz finished his exam. Let us celebrate!

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Good idea. How about Saturday evening?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Saturday is good for me. Where?

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: Why don't we go to the new restaurant near the park?

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: I would like that. I am going to reserve a table for six.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Would you like to invite Mr Karimov?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Yes! He helped me every week.

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: I am going to buy flowers and a small gift.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Sarah, can you pick up Mr Karimov at seven?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: I would love to. Let us meet at the restaurant at half past seven.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: That sounds good. Thank you!

body.speaker: narrator
body.text: Mr Karimov is at the doctor. Sarah is with him.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: How do you feel today?

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: I have a headache and a cough. I am not well.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: You should stay at home. You must not work this week.

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: But I have to teach! There are thirty students.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: You do not have to teach. I can do it.

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: Are you sure? That is a lot of work for you.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: I am sure. You should stay at home and rest.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: And you must not smoke. The doctor said that too.

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: You are right. Thank you. That is very kind of you.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Sarah, is London bigger than Tashkent?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Yes, it is. But Tashkent is bigger than my town.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Tashkent is the biggest city in Uzbekistan.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: And Samarkand? Is it as big as Tashkent?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: No, it is not as big. But it is much older.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Samarkand is more famous than Tashkent, I think.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: That is true. It is the most famous city here.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: In England the weather is worse. Here it is better!

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Summer here is hotter than summer in England.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Much hotter! But the winter is not as cold as ours.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: So this is the best country. Now you have to stay!
